name: publicWeb_getBlockedHashers
description: Web member's door to HC6.hcapp_getBlockedHashers (E9.F1.S16/S17): the member's blocked hashers, for the screen where a block is undone. Read-only. A thin wrapper that EXECs the app SP and returns its rowsets unchanged. Auth: the wrapped SP's HC6.ValidateAppAuth — token signed for hcapp_getBlockedHashers; scoped to the token's user.

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: The browser's HC.Device id (the web member session). No SQL default.

parameters.name: accessToken
parameters.description: Short-lived token signed for hcapp_getBlockedHashers (the SP that validates it). No SQL default.

rowsets.description: As returned by HC6.hcapp_getBlockedHashers: Auth failure (ValidateAppAuth) returns the error detail alone and the SP returns. No compact envelope.

rowsets.name: BlockedHashers
rowsets.description: As returned by HC6.hcapp_getBlockedHashers: On success: one row per blocked hasher, ORDER BY HasherFriendMap.updatedAt DESC. Empty when the caller has blocked nobody. WHERE f.UserId = @userId AND f.Ignore = 1 (no filter on f.Removed or h.Removed: a GDPR-deleted hasher still appears as 'Deleted User').

columns.name: PublicHasherId
columns.description: UPPER(CAST(Hasher.PublicHasherId AS NVARCHAR(40))) — the blocked hasher's public id in upper case; the app lowercases it on arrival (lowerGuidsInPlace).

columns.name: DisplayName
columns.description: Hasher.DisplayName — persisted computed column honouring NameDisplayPreference.

columns.name: BlockedAt
columns.description: HasherFriendMap.updatedAt — when the block was last set (column added by db/hc6/app/archive/2026-09-29_hasher_block.sql).

sideEffects: EXEC HC6.hcapp_getBlockedHashers with the same arguments — every side effect is the wrapped SP's:
None on success. INSERT HC.ErrorLog then THROW on an unhandled error (CATCH, line 48).
INSERT HC.ErrorLog ('<web>', userId NULL, deviceId) then THROW in the wrapper's CATCH, for an error the wrapped SP does not handle itself.

codeSmells.detail: @deviceId and @accessToken have no SQL default (line 14). A caller that omits one is refused by SQL Server before the procedure runs — an empty 500 with no HC.ErrorLog row (CLAUDE.md 'SP parameter with NO default'). The Next.js client always sends them, so this is latent.
The wrapped SP's CATCH logs to HC.ErrorLog and THROWs; this wrapper's CATCH (lines 23-28) catches the re-raise and logs a second row for the same failure.

breakingChangeRules: Never remove a column from any rowset
Never change a sentinel value meaning
Never change errorType integer codes without updating all callers
